result.topic_en: Euler derives an interpolation series for sin(ωπ)/sin(nπ) in two arbitrary numbers n and ω. In its limiting cases ω→0 and n→0 it yields series for π/sin(nπ), for π itself, and for sin(ωπ)/π.
result.transcription:
— 204 —
vnde deducuntur hae aequationes:
$\frac{f}{n} = A$
$\frac{f}{1-n} = A + B.1(1-2n)$
$\frac{-f}{1+n} = A + B.1(1+2n) + C.1(1+2n).2.2n$
$\frac{-f}{2-n} = A + B.2(2-2n) + C.2(2-2n).1(3-2n)$
$+ D.2(2-2n).1(3-2n).3(1-2n)$
etc.
hincque coefficientium valores sequentes:
$A = \frac{f}{n};\ B = \frac{-f}{n(1-n)};\ C = \frac{f}{2n(1-n)(1+n)};$
$D = \frac{-f}{6n(1-n)(1+n)(2-n)};\ E = \frac{f}{24n(1-n)(1+n)(2-n)(2+n)}$ [?]; etc.
quae progressio cum satis sit simplex, series nostra pro valore ipsius $y$, quem iam nouimus esse $= \frac{\sin.\omega\pi}{\sin.n\pi}$, eo maiorem attentionem meretur; haecque est
$\frac{\sin.\omega\pi}{\sin.n\pi} = \frac{\omega}{n} - \frac{\omega}{n}\cdot\frac{\omega\omega-nn}{1(1-n)} + \frac{\omega}{n}\cdot\frac{\omega\omega-nn}{1(1-n)}\cdot\frac{\omega\omega-(1-n)^2}{2(1+n)}$
$- \frac{\omega}{n}\cdot\frac{\omega\omega-nn}{1(1-n)}\cdot\frac{\omega\omega-(1-n)^2}{2(1+n)}\cdot\frac{\omega\omega-(1+n)^2}{3(2-n)} + \text{etc.}$
vel si $\Pi$ ingiter denotet terminum praecedentem, totum erit:
$\frac{\sin.\omega\pi}{\sin.n\pi} = \frac{\omega}{n} - \Pi.\frac{\omega\omega-nn}{1(1-n)} + \Pi.\frac{\omega\omega-(1-n)^2}{2(1+n)} - \Pi.\frac{\omega\omega-(1+n)^2}{3(2-n)}$
$+ \Pi.\frac{\omega\omega-(2-n)^2}{4(2+n)} - \Pi.\frac{\omega\omega-(2+n)^2}{5(3-n)} + \text{etc.}$
Quodsi omnes termini eodem signo affecti desiderentur, erit:
$\frac{\sin.\omega\pi}{\sin.n\pi} = \frac{\omega}{n} + \frac{\omega}{n}\cdot\frac{nn-\omega\omega}{1(1-n)} + \frac{\omega}{n}\cdot\frac{nn-\omega\omega}{1(1-n)}\cdot\frac{(1-n)^2-\omega\omega}{2(1+n)}$
$+ \frac{\omega}{n}\cdot\frac{nn-\omega\omega}{1(1-n)}\cdot\frac{(1-n)^2-\omega\omega}{2(1+n)}\cdot\frac{(1+n)^2-\omega\omega}{3(2-n)}$
$+ \frac{\omega}{n}\cdot\frac{nn-\omega\omega}{1(1-n)}\cdot\frac{(1-n)^2-\omega\omega}{2(1+n)}\cdot\frac{(1+n)^2-\omega\omega}{3(2-n)}\cdot\frac{(2-n)^2-\omega\omega}{4(2+n)}$
etc.
Haec series eo maiori attentione digna videtur, quod a foli-

— 205 —
folita serierum ratione plurimum recedit, in eaque adeo duo numeri arbitrarii $n$ et $\omega$ occurrunt.
Corollarium 1.
§. 53. Si numerus $\omega$ euanescat, vt fiat $\sin.\omega\pi = \omega\pi$, diuisione per $\omega$ instituta habebitur haec aequatio:
$\frac{\pi}{\sin.n\pi} = \frac{1}{n} + \frac{n}{1(1-n)} + \frac{n(1-n)}{1.2(1+n)} + \frac{n(1-n)(1+n)}{1.2.3(2-n)}$
$+ \frac{n(1-n)(1+n)(2-n)}{1.2.3.4(2+n)} + \text{etc.}$
vnde sumto $n = \frac{1}{2}$, ob $\sin.\frac{\pi}{2} = 1$ erit
$\pi = 2 + 1 + \frac{1.1}{2.4.3} + \frac{1.1.3.3}{2.4.4.6.5} + \frac{1.1.3.3.5.5}{2.4.4.6.6.8.7}$ [?] $+ \text{etc.}$
seu $\pi = 2 + \frac{\pi}{3}$ [?]
$+ 1 + \frac{1}{2.2^2.3} + \frac{1.3}{2.4.2^4.5} + \frac{1.3.5}{2.4.6.2^6.7} + \frac{1.3.5.7}{2.4.6.8.2^8.9}$ [?] etc.
quarum serierum posterior cum sit semissis prioris, erit summa posterioris $= \frac{\pi}{3}$, cuius quidem ratio inde est manifesta, quod sit
$\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{(1-xx)}} = \text{ang.}\sin.x = x + \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{x^3}{3} + \frac{1.3}{2.4}\cdot\frac{x^5}{5} + \frac{1.3.5}{2.4.6}\cdot\frac{x^7}{7} + \text{etc.}$
vnde illa series fit $= \frac{\text{ang.}\sin.x}{x}$, sumto $x = \frac{1}{2}$ ideoque $= 2\cdot\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3}$.
Corollarium 2.
§. 54. Si alter numerus $n$ euanescat, vt fiat $\sin.n\pi = n\pi$, et aequatio per $n$ multiplicetur, orietur:
$\frac{\sin.\omega\pi}{\pi} = \omega - \frac{\omega^3}{1} + \frac{\omega^3(\omega^2-1)}{1.2} - \frac{\omega^3(\omega^2-1)(\omega^2-1)}{1.2.3.2} + \frac{\omega^3(\omega^2-1)(\omega^2-1)(\omega^2-4)}{1.2.3.4.2.2}$ [?]
$- \frac{\omega^3(\omega^2-1)(\omega^2-1)(\omega^2-4)(\omega^2-4)}{1.2.3.4.5.2.2.3}$ [?] $+ \text{etc.}$
quae series per $\omega$ diuisa in binos sequentes resoluitur:
$\frac{\sin.\omega\pi}{\omega\pi} = 1 + \frac{\omega^2(\omega^2-1)}{1.2.1^2} + \frac{\omega^2(\omega^2-1)^2(\omega^2-4)}{1.2.3.4.1^2.2^2} + \frac{\omega^2(\omega^2-1)^2(\omega^2-4)^2(\omega^2-9)}{1.2.3.4.5.6.1^2.2^2.3^2}$ [?] $+ \text{etc.}$
$- \omega^2 - \frac{\omega^2(\omega^2-1)^2}{1.2.3.1^2.2}$ [?] $- \frac{\omega^2(\omega^2-1)^2(\omega^2-4)^2}{1.2.3.4.5.1^2.2^2.3}$ [?] $- \text{etc.}$
Cc 3 Summa-

items.quote: quae progressio cum satis sit simplex, series nostra pro valore ipsius $y$, quem iam nouimus esse $= \frac{\sin.\omega\pi}{\sin.n\pi}$, eo maiorem attentionem meretur
items.english: Since this progression is quite simple, our series for the value of y, which we already know to be sin ωπ / sin nπ, deserves all the more attention.

items.quote: quarum serierum posterior cum sit semissis prioris, erit summa posterioris $= \frac{\pi}{3}$
items.english: Since the latter of these series is half of the former, the sum of the latter will be π/3.
